output: rmarkdown::html_document

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE,comment='#>',message=FALSE,warning=FALSE)
```

Interaction effects describe how one predictor's association with the response
depends on another predictor. L0glm can generate these terms after selecting the
main effects, then repeat sparse selection on the expanded candidate set. This
keeps the working design manageable when there are many original predictors.

## Fit a model with interaction effects

`interactions` controls the stages of interaction generation:

| Setting | Candidate terms |
| --- | --- |
| `0L` | Main effects |
| `1L` | Main effects and pairwise products |
| `2L` | Also three-way products |

The default is `0L`. The following example includes signed main effects, a
pairwise interaction and a three-way interaction.

```{r interaction-fit}
library(L0glm)
set.seed(171)
X <- matrix(rnorm(300*12),300,12,dimnames=list(NULL,letters[1:12]))
y <- 1+2*X[,1]-2*X[,2]+2*X[,3]+2*X[,1]*X[,2]+
  2*X[,1]*X[,2]*X[,3]+rnorm(300)
fit <- l0glmFit(X,y,family=gaussian(),intercept=TRUE,lambda='gic',
  interactions=2L,relaxed=TRUE,dispersion=1)
fit$interactions$history
coef(fit)[which(Matrix::rowSums(coef(fit)!=0)>0),,drop=FALSE]
```

Only selected original main effects generate products. The two-way stage forms
pairwise products, and the next stage forms three-way products among the original
main effects still selected. Each predictor appears once per product. Intercepts
and compulsory terms remain main effects. All generated terms stay available in
subsequent stages, and subsequent selection can discard a parent main effect.

For named presets, the penalty is recalculated from the original selectable
predictor count plus the generated products. Stage scores use a common final
candidate count and the usual free-coefficient degrees of freedom. The best
stage is retained. A numeric `lambda` remains fixed across stages.

## Prediction and reproducibility

Prediction accepts the original main-effect columns and creates the products
it needs. Sparse inputs retain sparse storage. The model keeps a lightweight
training-design view, avoiding a second copy of all original columns.

```{r interaction-prediction}
predict(fit,X[1:5,])
fit$interactions$terms
```

The recipe includes the fitting specification, so the complete pipeline can be
repeated with the original data:

```{r interaction-repeat, eval=FALSE}
repeated <- do.call(l0glmFit,c(list(X=X,y=y),fit$interactions$specification))
```

Explicit starting-zero exclusions also constrain products in the corresponding
response channel. New products receive normalized-coordinate starts and prior
mean zero. Predictor groups are supported; products with the same tuple of
parent group labels form an interaction group.

## Cross-validation and validation stopping

```{r interaction-cv, eval=FALSE}
cv <- l0glmTune(X,y,family=gaussian(),intercept=TRUE,interactions=2L,
  tune='cv',nfolds=5L,nlambda=10L,relaxed=TRUE)
predict(cv$fit_1se,X[1:5,])
```

Every training fold selects its own main effects and generates its own products.
Full-data paths share a union of product rows for plotting, with zeros for terms
absent from a fit. Independent validation data can also choose the best stage:
pass `validation=list(X=V,y=v)`, using the original main-effect columns. Generation
stops when validation deviance worsens.

`control.interactions` bounds the candidate count and working-design size before
products are constructed. See [interaction models](../reference/interaction_models.html)
for the mathematical convention, controls and returned recipe.
